Rashi on Niddah 62a:11:1.hebrew: שנאן ועבר טהרותיו טהורות - דאם איתא דדם הוא, בהעברה קמייתא הוה עבר:
Rashi on Niddah 62a:11:1.english: [If] he repeated them and it disappeared, his pure items are pure - For if it were [so] that it is blood, it would have disappeared in the first application.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:12:1.english: Washing - The application of the substances.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:12:2.hebrew: שהרי הקפיד עליו - כשחזר והעבירן, גילה דעתו שמקפיד עליו בספק דם:
Rashi on Niddah 62a:12:2.english: For he was particular about it - When he went back and applied them [again], he revealed his mindset that he is particular about it regarding suspected blood:

Rashi on Niddah 62a:12:3.hebrew: ועבר - על ידי העברה זו, ונעשה בו מעשה דם, שכן דרך דם לעבור על ידי שבעה הסממנים:
Rashi on Niddah 62a:12:3.english: And it disappeared - [It disappeared] through this application [of the substances], and it exhibited the behavior of blood, for it is the nature of blood to disappear through the seven substances.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:1:1.english: Cimolian earth and potash - [These are] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:2:1.english: He immersed it - Before he applied them to it.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:2:2.hebrew: הרי זה צבע - דאי הוה דם, הוה עבר:
Rashi on Niddah 62a:2:2.english: This is dye - For if it were blood, it would have disappeared.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:2:3.english: That it faded - It changed from its redness.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:3:1.hebrew: לעיסת גריסין של פול חלוקת נפש - שנחלק האוכל מן הקליפה, לועסה לגריסת הפול ומעבירו על הכתם:
Rashi on Niddah 62a:3:1.english: Chewing of split beans of a fava bean that divided naturally - [Meaning] that the edible part was separated from the husk; one chews the split fava bean and applies it to the stain.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:4:2.hebrew: שלש פעמים - בין שתי ידיו, כדרך כיבוס בגדים, שכופל צדו עם צדו, ומשפשף ומוליך ומביא:
Rashi on Niddah 62a:4:2.english: Three times - Between his two hands, in the manner of laundering garments, where he folds one side against the other and rubs, moving [it] back and forth.

Rashi on Niddah 62a:4:3.english: In their order - In the order that they are taught here [in the mishna].

Rashi on Niddah 62a:4:4.english: He has done nothing - Neither to test [the stain] nor to nullify [it].

Rashi on Niddah 62a:7:1.english: They added to them - [This was taught] with regard to the Sabbatical Year: The halbitzin [bulbs of ornithogalum].

Rashi on Niddah 62a:7:2.english: A root - A root from which [the plant] lives. And sulfur is merely earth.

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:10:1.hebrew: צפון צבע נמי מעבר - וא"ת: ומה בכך? והא הקפיד עליו, כיון שהעביר צפון אחר שבעה סמנין; ונימא דטהרותיו טמאות דקאמר, קאי אתכבוסת שניה, ומהאי טעמא נמי קאמרינן לקמן שנאן ועבר, דטהרות שנעשו אחר תכבוסת שניה טמאות, והכא נמי ליטמא! וליכא למימר דקפידא לא מהני אלא כשעובר בז' סממנין שמעבירין בקל, אבל צפון שמעביר על ידי הדחק, אפילו הקפיד — טהורות; דלקמן מסיק רב פפא: יכול לצאת והקפיד עליו — דברי הכל טמא, אע"פ שאין יכול לצאת אלא ע"י הדחק. והיינו שיכול לצאת על ידי צפון, דהא ממתני' פריך רבי יוחנן לריש לקיש: אמאי טהורה כי לא עבר ע"י ז' סמנין? הא יכול לצאת ע"י צפון! וי"ל, דברייתא לא מיירי בטהרות דאחר תכבוסת שניה, דיותר היה ראוי לאשמועינן טהרותיו טהורות אטהרות דאחר תכבוסת ראשונה, כדקאמר בברייתא דלקמן; אלא אתכבוסת ראשונה נמי קאי. והוה מצי למפרך מברייתא דבסמוך דקתני: שנאן ועבר טהרותיו טהורות, אלא דניחא ליה למיפרך מגופה:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:10:1.english: Soap removes dye as well - And if you say: And what of it? Behold, he was particular about it, since he applied soap after the seven substances! And let us say that [the statement that] "his pure items are impure" refers to [items handled after] the second laundering; and for this reason as well we say below [regarding the case where] he repeated them and it disappeared, that [pure] items prepared after the second laundering are impure, so here too let them be impure? And one cannot say that being particular is effective only when [a stain] disappears through the seven substances, which remove [it] easily, but [as for] soap, which removes [it only] with difficulty, even if he was particular, [the pure items] are pure; for below, Rav Pappa concludes: "[If an absorbed substance] is able to emerge and he was particular about it, everyone agrees that it is impure," even though it is able to emerge only with difficulty. And that is [the case of being] able to emerge by means of soap, for from our mishna Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish: Why is [the garment] pure when [the stain] did not disappear through the seven substances? Behold, it is able to emerge by means of soap! And one can say: The baraita is not dealing with [the] pure items [handled] after the second laundering, for it would have been more appropriate to teach us [that] "his pure items are pure" regarding the pure items [handled] after the first laundering, as [the Tanna] states in the baraita below; rather, [the ruling that his pure items are impure] applies to the first laundering as well. And [the Gemara] could have raised an objection from the adjacent baraita, which teaches: "[If] he repeated them and it disappeared, his pure items are pure"; but it preferred to raise an objection from [the baraita] itself:

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:10:2.hebrew: העביר עליו ששה סמנין ולא עבר העביר עליו צפון ועבר כו' - תימה: פשיטא! והלא אינו מזכיר במשנתינו צפון במנין ז' סממנין, ומאי קא משמע לן? והא פשיטא דבששה לא סגי! ויש לומר, דאשמועינן דאע"ג דלא עבר כלל ולא נשתנה ע"י ו' סמנין, איכא למימר: משום השביעי לא יעבור; קא משמע לן דיש להחמיר, דשמא בשביעי, אם העביר קודם הצפון, היה עובר:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:10:2.english: [If] one applied six substances to it and it did not disappear, [and] applied soap to it and it disappeared, etc. - [This is] astonishing: [This is] obvious! For behold, [the Tanna] does not mention soap in our mishna among the tally of the seven substances, and what does [the baraita] come to teach us? For isn't it obvious that six [substances] do not suffice? And one can say that it teaches us that even though [the stain] did not disappear at all and did not change by means of the six substances, [such that] one might say that on account of the seventh it would not disappear, it comes to teach us that one must be stringent, for perhaps with the seventh, had he applied [it] prior to the soap, it would have disappeared.

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:11:1.hebrew: שנאן ועבר - נראה לר"י, דע"י שנאן צבע נמי עובר; דאי לאו הכי, אמאי טהורות אפילו למפרע? הא ליכא הכא ספק ספקא, ויהיו טמאות למפרע, כיון דליכא אלא חדא ספקא, כדפרישית במתניתין:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:11:1.english: [If] he repeated them and it disappeared - It appears to the Ri that through repeating them, dye also disappears; for if not so, why are [the ritually pure items] pure even retroactively? Behold, there is no compound doubt (safek sefeika) here, and they should be impure retroactively, since there is only a single doubt, as I explained in our Mishnah.

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:12:1.hebrew: שהרי הקפיד עליו - וא"ת אמתני' דקתני הרי זה צבע, מ"מ כשיכבסנו הרי מקפיד עליו, וליטמא טהרות דאחר תכבוסת? וי"ל דכבוס אינו קפידא, דאינו אלא ללבנו. וא"ת, מ"מ כשיכבסנו יטמא הבגד, שיצא הדם ואינו בלוע? וי"ל דביציאתו יבטל נמי בתכבוסת:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:12:1.english: For he was particular about it - And if you say regarding our mishna, which teaches, "That is a dye": Nevertheless, when he launders it, he is particular about it, so let it render impure the pure items [handled] after laundering! And one can say that laundering is not [considered] being particular, for it is only to whiten it [the garment]. And if you say: Nevertheless, when he launders it, the garment should become impure, for the blood will emerge and will no longer be absorbed! And one can say that upon its emergence, it is also nullified in the washing.

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:12:2.hebrew: שהרי הקפיד עליו ועבר - וא"ת, מה צריך לומר ועבר? וכי תימא משום דנפלט וטמא הבגד, א"כ אמאי נקט והקפיד? וי"ל, דנקט ועבר, דאז קפידתו קפידא, הואיל והועילה מחשבתו שעבר. ומשום הכי נמי קתני במתניתין, דכי לא עבר טהור, ואף על גב דהקפיד:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:12:2.english: For he was particular about it and it disappeared - And if you say: Why is it necessary to say "and it disappeared"? And should you say [that it is] because it was discharged and defiled the garment, if so, why did [Rabbi Zeira] state "and he was particular"? And one can say: That he stated "and it disappeared" because then his particularity is [considered] particularity, since his intention was effective in that it disappeared. And because of this as well, it teaches in the Mishnah that when it did not disappear, [the garment] is pure, even though he was particular.

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:2:1.hebrew: הטבילו ועשה על גביו טהרות כו' הרי זה צבע - אין לפרש: "הרי זה ודאי צבע", כדפירש בקונטרס בפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין דף מט:); דאם כן, לקמן אמאי קאמר: "אבל טהרות שאחר תכבוסת שניה טמאות"? הלא כיון שלא עבר מתחלה בז' סממנים, ודאי צבע הוא! ועוד, כי פריך לקמן לר"ל, דאמר: "בלוע שיכול לצאת ע"י הדחק לא שמיה בלוע", ממתניתין ד"הרי זה צבע" — מאי פירכא היא? הרי היא ודאי צבע, ואין כאן טומאה בלועה כלל! ואמאי נקט נמי "והטבילו"? אפי' לא הטבילו נמי! על כן צריך לפרש: "הרי זה ספק צבע", כלומר, יש לנו לתלות בצבע. ואע"פ דפעמים דדם נדה [אינו] עובר ע"י ז' סמנין, הכא איכא ספק ספקא, מלבד טעמא דבטול: דשמא צבע הוא, כיון דלא עבר; ואם תמצי לומר דדם הוא — אימא מעלמא אתא. הילכך, מטהרינן אפילו למפרע. אבל טעמא דבטול לחוד לא מהני, דגבי דם נדה דקאמר: "מעביר עליו ז' סמנין ומבטלו", אינו אלא לטהר מכאן ולהבא, אבל למפרע טמא מדרבנן, הואיל והקפיד, שסבור שיכול לצאת ע"י ז' סממנין ואכתי לא בטלו; ואע"ג דמן התורה טהור, דהואיל ואין סופו לצאת ע"י ז' סממנין נתבטל, אבל כאן, כיון דאיכא ספק ספקא ובטול, טהור אף מדרבנן למפרע. ומיהו, מטעם ספק ספקא לחוד לא הוה מטהרינן ליה אי לאו טעמא דבטול, משום דרגילות לבא דם מגופה, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא (לעיל נדה דף ג.): "בצפור לא נתעסקה, בשוק של טבחים לא עברה — האי דם מהיכא אתא?"; דעל כרחך בלא טעמא דבטול לא מטהרינן ליה מטעם ספק ספקא, מדנקט "הטבילו", אע"ג דמקילינן בשאר ספק ספקא. ומשום הכי פריך מינה לר"ל דבטל, אע"ג דיכול לצאת ע"י הדחק בצפון. ואם תאמר: אכתי למה לי "הטבילו", כיון דטהור מטעם בטול וספק ספקא? וי"ל, דנהי דכשנתייבש הבגד נתבטל, מיהו בעודו לח לא נתבטל, ובעודו לח נגע בו הבגד, ומשום הכי צריך להטביל. ועוד יש לומר: "הרי זה צבע" — צביעות דם בעלמא, ונתבטל, ולא נצטרך לטעם דספק ספקא. והשתא נתפרש טעם בטול במשנה, דמינה פריך לריש לקיש. ומיהו, פירוש ראשון נראה עיקר, דלשון "צבע" לא משמע צביעות דם, אלא צבע ממש:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:2:1.english: [If] one immersed it and handled ritually pure items upon it, etc., it is a dye - One should not explain [the words] "it is a dye" [to mean that] it is definitely dye, as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi] in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 49b); for if so, why does [the Gemara] say later on: "However, the pure items [handled] after the second washing are impure"? Behold, since it did not disappear initially with the seven substances, it is definitely a dye! And furthermore, when [Rabbi Yoḥanan] later objects to Reish Lakish — who says: "Absorbed [matter] that can emerge through forcing (al yedei hadeḥak) is not considered absorbed" — from our mishna of "it is a dye", what objection is that? Behold, it is definitely dye, and there is no absorbed impurity here at all! And why did [the mishna] also state "and he immersed it"? Even if he did not immerse it, [the items should] also [be pure]! Therefore, one must explain: "It is an uncertain dye" — that is to say, we are to attribute [the stain] to dye. And even though menstrual blood sometimes does [not] disappear through the seven substances, here there is a double doubt (safek sefeika), in addition to the reason of nullification (bittul): for perhaps it is dye, since it did not disappear; and if you say that it is blood, say that it came from elsewhere (me-alma). Therefore, we rule [the items] pure even retroactively. However, the reason of nullification alone would not be effective, for regarding menstrual blood, where [Rabbi Ḥiyya] says, "one applies the seven substances to it and nullifies it," it is only to purify from here on and onward; but retroactively, it is impure rabbinically, since he was particular [about it], believing that it could emerge through the seven substances, and had not yet nullified it; and even though by Torah law it is pure — since it will not ultimately emerge through the seven substances, it became nullified — nevertheless, here, since there is a double doubt and nullification, it is pure even rabbinically retroactively. However, based on the reason of a double doubt alone we would not rule it pure were it not for the reason of nullification, because blood is accustomed to come from her body, as we say in the first chapter (above, Niddah 3a): "[If] she was not involved with a bird, and she did not pass through a butchers' market — from where did this blood come?"; for perforce, without the reason of nullification we would not rule it pure on the basis of a double doubt, from the fact that [the mishna] stated "and he immersed it", even though we are lenient in other cases of double doubt. And on account of this, [Rabbi Yoḥanan] objects from it to Reish Lakish that [the blood] is nullified even though it can emerge through forcing with soap (tzafon). And if you say: Still, why do I need [the mishna to state] "and he immersed it", since it is pure by virtue of nullification and double doubt? And one can say: Granted that when the garment dried [the stain] became nullified; however, while it was still wet it was not nullified, and while it was still wet the garment came into contact with it, and for this reason it was necessary to immerse [the garment]. And furthermore, one can say: "It is a dye" [means] mere discoloration of blood, and it was nullified, and we do not need the reason of double doubt. And now, the reason of nullification is stated explicitly in the mishna, from which [Rabbi Yoḥanan] objects to Reish Lakish. However, the first explanation appears primary, for the term "dye" (tzeva) does not imply the discoloration of blood, but rather actual dye.

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:6:1.hebrew: אמר רב יהודה זה אהל - בשבת פרק רבי עקיבא (שבת דף צ.), איכא ספרים דגרסי: זה החול, ופריך: והתניא הבורית והחול? ותימה, דהתנן חול בפרק המוציא (שם פ:)! וי"ל, דתרי גווני חול: חד לבנין, וחד לחפיפה וכבוס. ואתי שפיר לההיא גירסא במסקנא, דקאמר: אלא מאי בורית אהל, ולא קאמר: אלא לעולם כו':
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:6:1.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is ahal [ice plant] - In [Tractate] Shabbat, in chapter "Rabbi Akiva" (Shabbat 90a), there are texts that read: "This is sand," and [the Gemara there] objects: "Was it not taught: Borit and sand?" And this is astonishing, for didn't we learn [the measure for] sand in chapter "HaMotsi" (ibid. 80b)? And it can be said that there are two types of sand: one for building, and one for hair-washing and laundering. And according to that reading, it works out well that in the conclusion it says, "Rather, what is borit? Ahal," and does not say, "Rather, actually [it is as stated initially], etc."

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:6:2.hebrew: והתניא הבורית והאהל - פי' לענין שביעית נשנית. אבל לפי גירסת הספרים דשבת, דגרס הבורית והחול, תימה היא: לענין מה נשנית? ואי לענין הוצאת שבת, הא קאמר רבי יהודה שיעור בנתר ובורית כדי להעביר בו את הכתם, והך שיעורא לא שייך רק מהני ז' מיני סמנים. ומיהו אפשר דרבנן אית להו דבורית וחול, הראויין לחפיפה וכבוס, אית להו חד שיעורא לענין שבת, ורבי יהודה פליג אבורית לחוד וקאמר כדי להעביר בו את הכתם:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:6:2.english: But isn't it taught: Borit and ahal - Explanation: [This baraita] was taught regarding [the laws of] the Sabbatical year. But according to the reading of the books in Shabbat, which read "borit and sand," it is puzzling: Regarding what matter was it taught? And if [it was taught] regarding carrying out on Shabbat, behold, Rabbi Yehuda says [that the] measure for natron and borit is [sufficient] to remove the stain with it, and this measure applies only to these seven types of substances [that remove stains]! However, it is possible that the Rabbis maintain that borit and sand, which are suitable for hair washing and laundering, have one [and the same] measure regarding Shabbat, and Rabbi Yehuda disputes [them] regarding borit alone, and says: "[sufficient] to remove the stain with it."

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:6:3.hebrew: כבריתא - פירש"י: גפרית. וכן בערוך: אש וגפרית, תרגום: אשתא וכבריתא (תהילים י״א:ו׳). והקשה הר"ר יעקב מאורליינ"ש: בשבת, כי פריך כבריתא מי אית ליה שביעית, לפרוך ממתני' דשבת, דתנן בפ' המוציא (דף עח:) שיעור אחרינא בגפרית וזפת: כדי לסתום נקב. ומיהו לא קשה, דבכמה מקומות מצי למפרך ממשנה, וכשהפירכא יותר פשוטה מן הברייתא, פריך מינה. ועוד, כיון שסידר הש"ס הכא, הובאה שם והוקבעה:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:6:3.english: Sulfur [khavrita] - Rashi explains: Sulfur [gophris]. And similarly in the Arukh: [Regarding] "fire and sulfur," the Targum translates [it as] "eishta ve-khavrita" (Psalms 11:6). And Rabbeinu Ya'akov of Orleans questioned: In [tractate] Shabbat, when [the Gemara] challenges: "Does sulfur have [the sanctity of] the Sabbatical Year?", let it challenge from the mishna in Shabbat [itself], as we learned in the chapter "HaMotzi" (78b) a different measure for sulfur and pitch: [an amount sufficient] to seal a hole! However, this is not difficult, for in many places [the Gemara] could challenge from a mishna, but when the challenge from the baraita is more straightforward, it challenges from it. And furthermore, since the Talmud arranged [this discussion] here [in tractate Niddah], it was brought there [to tractate Shabbat] and established [there].

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:7:1.hebrew: כל שאין לו עיקר - פירש בקונטרס במסכת עבודה זרה (דף יד.): עיקר המתקיים בארץ בימות החמה ובימות הגשמים. וזה קשה, דא"כ תבואה לא יהא נוהג בה שביעית, שאינה מתקיימת בימות הגשמים. ונראה כמו שפירש הכא, שאין לו שורש בארץ, כמו גפרית. וגם מה שפירש שם, תורניתא מין ארז, כדאיתא בראש השנה (דף כג.) שיטה תורניתא — זה אינו נראה; דבמסכת ע"ז (דף יד.) פריך כי הכא: ומי אית ליה שביעית? והתניא כו'. והרי ודאי לארז יש לו שורש! על כן נראה כמו שפי' רש"י בשבת (דף צ.), שהוא כעין מחפורת צריף שקורין אלו"ם, ומין קרקע הוא, וכמו גפרית הוא שאינו נשרש בארץ:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:7:1.english: Anything that does not have a root - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained in Tractate Avodah Zarah (14a) [that "root" means] a root that endures in the earth during the summer days and during the rainy days. And this is difficult, for if so, the Sabbatical Year would not apply to grain, which does not endure [in the ground] during the rainy season. And it appears [correct] as he explained here: that it has no root in the earth, like sulfur. And also what he explained there, that tornita is a type of cedar, as is found in Rosh Hashanah (23a), "shitta, tornita" — this does not appear [correct], for in Tractate Avodah Zarah (14a), [the Gemara] challenges just as [it does] here: "And does it have [sanctity of] the Sabbatical Year? But isn't it taught, etc.?" And surely a cedar tree has a root! Therefore, it appears as Rashi explained in Shabbat (90a), that it is like a quarry of tzrif, which is called alum, and it is a type of earth, and like sulfur, it does not take root in the earth.

Tosafot on Niddah 62a:7:2.hebrew: תרי גווני אהלא - תימה לספרים דגרסי בשבת (שם) והתניא הבורית והחול, אמאי לא משני מעיקרא תרי גווני חול, כדמשני במסקנא גבי אהל? וי"ל, דקים ליה להש"ס דלא הוו תרי גווני חול לכבוס:
Tosafot on Niddah 62a:7:2.english: Two types of ahala [ice plant] - It is puzzling according to the texts that read in Shabbat (ibid.): "And isn't it taught: The borit and the sand?" — why does [the Gemara] not answer initially [that there are] two types of sand, as it answers in the conclusion regarding ahal? And it can be answered that it was clear to the Gemara that there are not two types of sand [used] for laundering.
